title: Schuss Mountain Trail Map
html:
Welcome to one of Michigan’s top ski destinations—where terrain, trails, and fun come together at Schuss Mountain, Shanty Creek Resort.

Trail Overview | Schuss Mountain offers a variety of trails for all skill levels. Whether you’re a beginner or an expert, you’ll find groomed runs, glades, terrain parks, and great views across the mountain.

Trail Difficulty | Symbol | Description
Easiest | ● Green Circle | Wide, gentle slopes perfect for beginners
Intermediate | ♦ Blue Square | More challenging runs for developing skiers
Difficult | ◆ Black Diamond | Steeper, narrower, and faster terrain
Most Difficult | ⯁ Double Black Diamond | Expert terrain with steep drops and glades

Lifts - Schuss Mountain is equipped with a variety of lifts to help you access all areas of the resort efficiently:

  • Purple Lift – Access to beginner/intermediate terrain
  • Red Lift – Access to terrain park and advanced runs
  • Yellow Lift – Connects to summit trails
  • Surface Lifts – Perfect for beginners and ski school zones

Terrain Parks - Test your skills or try something new:

  • Low Rider Terrain Park – Features jumps, rails, and boxes for freestyle riders

  • Progression Zones – Great for learning tricks safely

Key Areas

  • Schuss Village – Base area with day lodge, rentals, tickets, ski school, and food
  • The Pink Lift Corner – Connects with multiple trail zones for diverse runs
  • Cedar River Village – Offers ski-in/ski-out access and lodging
  • Ski Patrol – Located near key intersections for safety and assistance

Tips for Visitors

  • Start your day early for fresh corduroy runs
  • Green trails near the base are best for families and beginners
  • Use lift maps and signage to plan your route across the mountain
  • Helmets are recommended for all riders

Download full trail map: Schuss Mountain Trail Map PDF

title: Nordic Trail Map
html:
Explore the snow-covered beauty of Shanty Creek Resort through its scenic Nordic ski and snowshoe trails. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced skier, these trails offer a peaceful and invigorating way to enjoy winter across Schuss Mountain.

Trail Overview
Trail Name | Distance (km) | Difficulty | Trail Use
Mountain Creek | 2.5 km | ● Moderate | Cross-country skiing
Poets Loop | 4.5 km | ● Moderate | Cross-country skiing
Pine Cone | 4.5 km | ◆ Difficult | Cross-country skiing
Winter Brook | 1.5 km | ● Moderate | Cross-country skiing
King of the Hill | 1.5 km | ◆ Difficult | Cross-country skiing
Schuss Mountain | 3.0 km | ● Easiest | Multi-purpose (snowshoe & bike)

Trail Markings
  • ⬤ Easiest
  • ● Moderate
  • ◆ Difficult
  • ⬛ Trail Head
  • Aa Landmarks

Each trail is clearly marked with signage and trailhead icons for convenience.

Village-to-Village Adventure

Many of these trails connect Schuss Mountain Village to surrounding areas like Cedar River Village, providing a “village-to-village” Nordic experience. You’ll pass iconic spots like Riverview, Red Lift Corner, and #3 Tee, making your trek both scenic and exciting.

Hours of Operation

  • Mon, Thurs, Fri: 9am – 4pm
  • Sat–Sun: 9am – 5pm
  • Closed: Tues & Wed
  • Holiday hours may vary

Ready to explore the trails?

title: Cross Country Skiing
html:
Few activities showcase the beauty of northern Michigan quite like cross country skiing. Shanty Creek’s 18km of groomed, track-set trails crisscross the four villages of the resort to create a “village-to-village” experience whose benefits include staying warm in winter, a heart-healthy cardio workout, and a beautiful setting. If Nordic skiing isn’t your thing, there is a 3km groomed multi-purpose trail at Schuss Village designated for fat tire biking and snowshoeing. This trail helps ensure skiers and bikers avoid accidents and unforeseen trail damage.

title: Alpine Tubing
html:
If skiing and snowboarding aren’t your thing—don’t worry! There’s still a fast and fun way to enjoy the snow. Alpine Tubing at Summit Mountain is a must-try winter activity, delivering all the thrills of sledding without the uphill climb.

You’ll hear laughter echoing across the slopes as guests of all ages race down the tubing lanes and ride the surface lift right back to the top. No skills required—just hold on and enjoy the ride!

🎯 What to Know:

  • Available Friday evenings, Saturdays, Sundays & holidays

  • Sessions start at the top of every hour

  • $25/hour on weekends and holidays, $23/hour on non-weekend days

  • Online booking only

  • Participants must be 36″ tall

💡 Parents Note:
The last two hours on Friday and Saturday nights are recommended for Adults Only—ideal for grown-ups looking to enjoy some child-free fun.

Whether you're with friends, family, or flying solo, Alpine Tubing offers a unique and laughter-filled way to enjoy Shanty Creek’s winter wonderland.

More info & booking: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/more-on-the-snow/#tubing

title: Snowshoeing
html:
Forge Your Own Trail – Adventure Awaits

Whether you're a seasoned snowshoer or trying it for the first time, snowshoeing at Shanty Creek offers a peaceful and scenic way to explore the winter woods of northern Michigan.

Slip on a pair and start walking—no special skills required. You can blaze your own path through the snowy landscape or follow the groomed 3km multi-purpose trail located at Schuss Village, shared with fat tire bikers and designed to minimize trail damage while keeping everyone safe.

Rental Equipment is available at the Nordic Center in Schuss Village, including snowshoes and poles.

This is a perfect winter activity for those seeking quiet beauty, fresh air, and an easy-going workout.

More Info: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/more-on-the-snow/

title: Snow Glide Tours
html:
Experience winter like never before with Shanty Creek’s Snow Glide Tours — a scenic, cozy, and memorable ride for all ages.

Departing from The Lakeview Hotel's front circle, this 45-minute guided tour winds through the snow-blanketed landscapes of Summit Village, offering sweeping views and a peaceful winter retreat without breaking a sweat. Whether you're snapping photos or simply soaking in the scenery, it’s the perfect way to appreciate the magic of northern Michigan in winter.

Each tour accommodates up to 9 passengers and is safely pulled behind “Big Blue,” a powerful double-track snowmobile. The Snow Glide is equipped with seatbelts for a secure and comfortable ride.

Tour Schedule:

  • Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and select holiday dates

  • Departures on the hour from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM

Price: $25 per seat
Limited availability – early booking is highly recommended!

More Info & Booking: https://www.shantycreek.com/snow-glide-tours/

title: Torch Lake
html:
📍 Torch Lake Township Info

Just a short drive from your stay, Torch Lake offers legendary turquoise waters and world-class fishing opportunities. From casting for bass and perch in shallow bays to trolling deep for lake trout or salmon, this lake is an angler’s dream.

• What You Can Catch: Trout, bass, pike, salmon, perch & more
• Best Spots: Northern drop-offs, rocky points, and deeper waters
• Access Points: Torch Lake Township Day Park, Torch River Bridge DNR Launch
• Need Help? Local fishing charters are available for guided adventures

Fishing Highlights

Torch Lake is a premier destination for fishing enthusiasts of all levels:

  • Lake Trout – thrive in the cold, deep waters.
  • Smallmouth & Largemouth Bass – plentiful along rocky points and weed beds.
  • Northern Pike & Muskellunge – trophy-sized catches possible near drop-offs.
  • Yellow Perch & Rock Bass – perfect for family-friendly fishing.
  • Salmon & Whitefish – migrate seasonally from connected waters.

For guided fishing trips, check out local charters such as:

  • Marty’s Torch Lake Guide Service (Bellaire, MI)
  • Captain Ron’s Fishing Charters (Elk Rapids, MI)

title: Clam Lake
html:
Website: https://watershedcouncil.org/waterbody/clam-lake/

A connecting lake that flows between Torch and Bellaire, Clam Lake offers excellent fishing for panfish, perch, and bass. Guests enjoy fishing from the shores of Clam River, which feeds the lake and is a hotspot for casting. Because it’s smaller and calmer than the big lakes, it’s ideal for kayaks and smaller boats.

Bellaire Police Department
Non-Emergency Phone: (231) 533-5678
Address: 202 N. Bridge St., Bellaire, MI 49615 (inside Community Hall)
Fax: (231) 533-8753
Chief of Police: Bill Drollinger; community-trained officers provide First Aid, AED, and CPR services.

This full-service department operates from within the Community Hall. Staff—trained in Basic First Aid, CPR, and the use of AEDs—offers patrol, law enforcement, community watch (including vacation property checks), and peace-of-mind services to ensure guest security. Village of Bellaire
